headline: Tether's engagements hit 79.8x baseline, nearly 3x Binance's own peak, as freezes took over
dek: Within 41 minutes of the sweep, the story was also about what stablecoin issuers could stop. The freeze became the night's second-largest theme and the main thing official accounts had to say.
narrative: The issuers' freezes turned a wallet drain into a second story. Tether's topic, normally about 33.4K engagements an hour, reached 2.7M in the 22:00 UTC hour: 79.8 times baseline, the highest multiple of the topics tracked and nearly three times Binance's 27.5x peak. USDC rose 14.0x by 00:00, to 5.1M an hour; Tether's base is small, and in absolute terms USDC added more per hour.

The freeze figures arrived before Binance spoke. @TreeNewsFeed posted "TETHER FREEZES $971M USDT" at 21:05 (2.0M), @WatcherGuru repeated it at 21:08 (605K), Whale Alert logged an address holding 971,149,299 USDT as frozen at 21:11, and WatcherGuru reported Circle freezing $823M of USDC at 21:13 (326K). Binance's first post came at 21:15.

The figure climbed by source. @WazzCrypto put the combined total at $1.8B at 21:12; Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said at 21:25 that Tether "froze more than 1.567B USDT" (1.03M); Binance said at 23:22 that "the current verified total frozen is $2.54 billion" (529K), and at 00:52 "around $3 billion" (156K).

In the 686 sampled posts, the freeze theme drew 188 posts and 21.2M engagements, second only to "hack / drained" (43.4M) and ahead of "largest ever" (12.2M) and "SAFU / funds safe" (9.5M); 103 of the 188 landed in the 21:00 hour.

The freeze gave the official accounts their script. CZ's 21:15 post (3.2M) thanked Tether ($971M) and Circle ($823M) in its second sentence. Yi He (@heyibinance) thanked Tether at 21:26 and 21:36, Ripple for freezing "approximately 200 million" at 22:08 (99.7K) and World Liberty Financial for $27M of USD1 at 22:22 (117K). @ZachWitkoff's USD1 freeze note reached 264K.

A counter-narrative ran alongside. @NPC_68 (253K on a 3.2K-follower account) wrote at 21:06 that the attacker was borrowing ETH on Aave against USDT: "USDT can be frozen by Tether. ETH can't." @BalaiBB made the same point at 22:09 (451K). Per on-chain checks reported by CryptoTicker, about 195,460 ETH sat untouched in a separate address as of 01:11 UTC and roughly 700M USDT moved before the freeze; Aave froze its USDT market (per @WatcherGuru, 21:52, 222K).

Tether's audience and tone shifted most. Over 24 hours its active creators rose from 486 to 1,985 and first-time posters from 261 to 1,694; from 20:00 to 00:59 UTC first-time posters ran 27.3x baseline. Tether's sentiment fell from 83 to 59 at 22:00 and was 65 at 00:00; USDC's moved from 85 to between 71 and 78. Over 24 hours USDT's price slipped 0.1 percent; USDC's was flat.

callouts.title: The freeze headline beat the exchange
callouts.body: Tether's $971M freeze was on X at 21:05, ten minutes before Binance posted, and drew 2.0M engagements. Binance and CZ adopted the freeze in their own messaging within minutes. Issuers acted as first responders in the public record.

callouts.title: Frozen totals are not one number
callouts.body: The frozen figure moved from $971M (21:05) to $1.8B combined (21:12), 1.567B USDT from Tether alone (21:25), Binance's $2.54B (23:22) and then about $3B (00:52), each from a different source and scope.
